solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Belt spread by a big starter of linguine and a crumbly dessert (10)

indicators.note: the belt is stretched around the other letters
the letters fall apart and re-form

blocks.note: a belt of land is a zone; it opens after Z

blocks.clueFragment: a big starter of linguine and a
blocks.note: A, BIG, L (first letter of linguine) and A, rearranged

annotation.surface: A diner's waistband strains after a big plate of pasta and a crumbly pudding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Belt' reads as the waistband being let out, but it is ZONE, split to hold the jumbled letters. Zabaglione is an Italian custard dessert of whipped egg yolks, sugar and Marsala.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain definition by category: this whipped custard of egg yolks and Marsala is served as a pudding.

entries.clue: Unsolicited correspondence from naked hunky male in prison (4,4)

indicators.note: stripped of its outer layer, so HUNKY loses its first and last letters
the pieces sit inside the prison

blocks.note: jail = prison; it wraps the rest

annotation.surface: A prisoner receives unwanted letters from a naked, hunky man.
annotation.walkthrough: The racy surface about a hunky male is a cover: 'naked' only strips a word of its outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Junk mail is unsolicited post, usually advertising.

entries.clue: Graphic extra disturbed duke (1-5)

indicators.note: the letters of EXTRA are disturbed into a new order

annotation.surface: A film extra playing a disturbed duke gets a graphic scene.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Graphic' looks like a design word; here it means explicit, as films are rated.
annotation.definitionFit: An X-rated film is graphic, with explicit sex or violence.

entries.clue: Bohemian family turning up after “blow” (7)

indicators.note: in a down answer, the word is read upwards
family comes after the blow

blocks.note: to beat is to strike a blow

annotation.surface: A bohemian's relatives turn up after someone has had a blow.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'blow' hint at slang for a drug, fitting a bohemian, but the word only means a hit.
annotation.definitionFit: A near-synonym: the 1950s Beat Generation drop-outs were the bohemians of their day, rejecting conventional dress and careers.

entries.clue: Patience of a sort shown by poor donkey supporting King Log’s head (8)

indicators.note: DONKEY is in poor shape and rearranged
in a down answer, the donkey sits below King and L

annotation.surface: A poor donkey holds up King Log's head, a fable scene.
annotation.walkthrough: Patience is the card game called solitaire in the US; Klondike is its best-known form. King Log is a character from Aesop, so the capital hides K + L.
annotation.definitionFit: Klondike (also spelt Klondyke) is a type of patience, the one-player card game.

entries.clue: Tiny bird, mostly cold, standing on hot drinking cup (6)

indicators.note: most of the word, so QUAIL loses its last letter
in a down answer, C sits on top of H

blocks.note: QUAIL, a small game bird, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A little bird, chilled, perches on a hot drinking cup.
annotation.walkthrough: A quaich is a shallow two-handled Scottish drinking bowl, often used for whisky.
annotation.definitionFit: A quaich is a Scottish shallow drinking cup with two handles.

entries.clue: Grain alcohol cleared out after case of misadventure (4)

indicators.note: ALCOHOL emptied of its middle leaves AL
'after' is read literally as following in time, so in the written answer the alcohol letters follow the misadventure letters
the outside letters of misadventure

annotation.surface: Someone's drink store has been emptied after a mishap.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grain alcohol' sits together as a phrase in the surface, but the definition stops after 'Grain'.
annotation.definitionFit: Meal is coarsely ground grain, as in oatmeal.

entries.clue: Shooting pioneer from Germany before a Napoleonic war? (8)

indicators.note: 'before' means ahead of, so in an across answer Germany's letter is written ahead of the war

blocks.note: D = Germany, its international vehicle code (Deutschland)
guerre is French for war, so a war Napoleon would name

annotation.surface: A gun pioneer from Germany ahead of a war in Napoleon's time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' means taking photographs, not firing; Louis Daguerre invented the daguerreotype. The question mark flags that 'Napoleonic' just means French.
annotation.definitionFit: Daguerre was a French pioneer of photography, whose daguerreotype was an early process.

entries.clue: Press plugs French articles, those offering an expanded view? (6)

indicators.note: the press fills a gap inside the articles, like a plug

blocks.note: les = the (plural) in French; it wraps OUP

annotation.surface: A news outlet promotes French articles that offer a broader perspective.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plugs' reads as advertises, which suits a press, but here it means fills a hole. A loupe is a jeweller's magnifying glass.
annotation.definitionFit: Loupes are small magnifying lenses, so they give an enlarged view.

entries.clue: Samsung finally takes recycled packing material (6)

indicators.note: the last letter of Samsung
G takes on the rest after it
TAKES is remade into a new order

annotation.surface: Samsung at last starts using recycled packaging.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is corporate green news; 'packing' here is engineering, the seal in a joint rather than a box's padding.
annotation.definitionFit: A gasket is packing material that seals the joint between two surfaces.

entries.clue: Spreadsheet item perhaps checks new private overseas asset (8)

definitions.note: TANGIBLE is used as a noun here: a tangible asset.

indicators.note: to check is to hold back, so TABLE restrains the letters inside it

blocks.note: a table is one thing a spreadsheet may hold; it wraps the rest
a GI is a private soldier in the US army

annotation.surface: An accountant's spreadsheet checks a new private asset held abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: The accounting surface makes 'checks' look like audits, but it means holds in. 'Overseas' tells you the private is American, a GI.
annotation.definitionFit: A tangible is a physical asset, such as property or equipment.

entries.clue: Undersized jumper in raffle artefacts (4)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words

annotation.surface: A child's small sweater turns up among the raffle prizes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater, as in British English, but it is an insect that jumps.
annotation.definitionFit: A flea is a tiny insect famous for jumping.

entries.clue: Assembly of plant components is in 24 hours transforming China (5,5)

indicators.note: 'in' is read as located within, so IS is placed within the letters for a day
CHINA is transformed into a new order

blocks.note: a day is 24 hours; it wraps IS

annotation.surface: A factory assembling parts is transforming China round the clock.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is manufacturing, but the 'plant components' are flowers: daisies threaded stem to stem.
annotation.definitionFit: A daisy chain is a string of daisies joined by their stems.

entries.clue: Absurd old tax collectors, extremely artful, limiting allowance (10)

indicators.note: the extreme letters of artful
IR and AL form the limits on either side of RATION

blocks.note: IR = Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority
a ration is a fixed allowance

annotation.surface: Old tax collectors were absurdly crafty about capping allowances.
annotation.walkthrough: The two outer pieces come from different parts of the clue yet act as one pair of bookends. The Inland Revenue merged into HMRC in 2005, hence 'old'.
annotation.definitionFit: Irrational means absurd, lacking reason.

entries.clue: Solemn, like a member of Parliament (6)

blocks.note: solemn = grave and wise-looking, the air of a certain night bird
a parliament is the collective noun for owls

annotation.surface: An MP is described as grave and serious.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital P makes you think of Westminster; a parliament is also a group of owls.
annotation.definitionFit: Owlish describes a solemn, bespectacled wise look, and literally means like an owl.

entries.clue: Composer butchers works (8)

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new shape

annotation.surface: A composer mangles his pieces.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Butchers' looks like the verb and 'works' like the noun; the jobs are the other way round.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Franz Schubert, the Austrian writer of lieder and symphonies, is one instance of a composer.

entries.clue: Note singer delivered (6)

indicators.note: a singer's line is delivered by voice, so we hear it

blocks.note: a tenor is a male singer

annotation.surface: A vocalist's musical note is sung.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'Note' a sound; it is a banknote. A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
annotation.definitionFit: A tenner is a ten-pound (or ten-dollar) note.

entries.clue: I so managed to be upset about small flowers (8)

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down
the reversed letters go around S

blocks.note: sic is Latin for thus, so
ran = managed, as in ran a shop

annotation.surface: Someone contrives to be upset about some small flowers.
annotation.walkthrough: The Latin word editors print in brackets to mean 'thus written' is the one that stands for 'so'; the whole string is then turned upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: Narcissi is the plural of narcissus, the daffodil family of flowers.

entries.clue: Female picked up ne’er-do-well, one having fine teeth? (7)

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifted means read upwards

annotation.surface: A woman picks up a layabout who has lovely teeth.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the teeth are a saw's, not a smile.
annotation.definitionFit: A fretsaw is a fine-toothed saw for cutting curves in thin wood.

entries.clue: Incidental series of changes including epitaph by that woman (10)

indicators.note: PEAL takes the other letters inside it
'by' in its sense of next to, as in a house by the sea, so that woman stands right beside the epitaph

blocks.note: in bell-ringing a peal is a long series of changes; it wraps the rest
RIP, rest in peace, is carved on gravestones

annotation.surface: A woman's epitaph gets revised several times as a side issue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Changes' are bell-ringing sequences, the orders in which a set of bells is rung.
annotation.definitionFit: Peripheral means incidental, of minor importance.

entries.clue: Goddess of Wrath, simmering, somewhat shown up (6)

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used
in a down answer, the letters read upwards

annotation.surface: A deity of fury, seething, is partly revealed.
annotation.walkthrough: Ishtar was the Babylonian goddess of love and war, so 'Goddess of Wrath' is nearly her real title.
annotation.definitionFit: Ishtar was the chief goddess of Babylon and Assyria.

entries.clue: Very porous clay he pounded (6)

indicators.note: pounded clay is broken up and re-formed

annotation.surface: A potter pounds a very porous clay.
annotation.walkthrough: Leachy soil lets water drain straight through it.
annotation.definitionFit: Leachy means porous, allowing liquid to leach through.

entries.clue: Tedious course associated with hard old book (4)

indicators.note: things associated with each other keep company, so the hard letter is attached straight after the tedious course

blocks.note: a rut is a dull routine

annotation.surface: A dull course is linked with a difficult old textbook.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old book' means a book of the Old Testament, not an antique.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example with a twist: 'old' means Old Testament, and this short story of a Moabite widow is one of its books.

entries.clue: Wager on dominant basic principles (8)

indicators.note: in an across answer, BET is placed on (after) ALPHA

blocks.note: the alpha in a group is the dominant one

annotation.surface: A gambler puts money on the favourite.
annotation.walkthrough: The betting surface hides a figurative sense: the alphabet of a subject is its ABC, its rudiments.
annotation.definitionFit: The alphabet of a subject means its basic principles, its ABC.

entries.clue: Covers of instruction books essentially bearing large print (4)

indicators.note: the outer letters of instruction
the essence, or middle, of books
in a down answer, IN and O carry L on top

annotation.surface: The covers of manuals carry large type.
annotation.walkthrough: BOOKS has an even count, so 'essentially' takes one of its two central Os. A lino is short for linocut, a print from carved linoleum.
annotation.definitionFit: A lino is a linocut, a print made from a carved block of linoleum.

entries.clue: Writer’s answer is about films being cut by 50pc (6)

indicators.note: 'about' as in about-turn: the word that follows faces the other way
half of MOVIES is cut away

blocks.note: MOVIES with its second half removed

annotation.surface: A screenwriter's reply is about films being slashed by half.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay. Isaac Asimov wrote science fiction.
annotation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov was a prolific science-fiction writer.

entries.clue: Dishonest amusement park opening late (6)

indicators.note: the opening letter is late, that is gone

annotation.surface: A crooked theme park opens behind schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Late' reads as delayed but means dead, gone, so the funfair loses its opening letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: unfair play is cheating, so dishonest dealing is unfair dealing.

entries.clue: Displaying loss of communication, desperate Appalachians without plan (8)

indicators.note: the remaining letters are in a desperate jumble
the letters of PLAN are taken out

blocks.note: APPALACHIANS minus P, L, A, N

annotation.surface: Hopeless hikers in the Appalachians, with no plan, lose contact.
annotation.walkthrough: Aphasia is loss of the ability to use or understand language, usually after brain damage.
annotation.definitionFit: Aphasiac describes someone with aphasia, who has lost language ability.
